bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to environment; establishing a rebate program to replace time-based ion exchange water softeners with demand-based ion exchange water softeners; appropriating money.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1. TIME-BASED WATER SOFTENER REPLACEMENT PROGRAM.

Subdivision 1.

Definitions.

(a) For purposes of this section, the following terms have the meanings given.

(b) "Contractor" means a Minnesota licensed plumber, water conditioning contractor, or installer.

(c) "Eligible replacement" means the replacement of a time-based ion exchange water softener with a demand-based ion exchange water softener that:

(1) softens incoming water of a hardness exceeding ten US grains per gallon to less than one US grain per gallon;

(2) has a salt efficiency greater than 3,500 grains per pound of salt; and

(3) is installed by a contractor between July 1, 2025, and June 30, 2027.

(d) "Rebate" means a rebate of $200, regardless of the size or cost of the work performed, equipment replaced, and equipment installed.

Subd. 2.

Rebate program.

The commissioner of the Pollution Control Agency must establish a program to provide rebates to the owner or lessee of a residential or commercial building who makes an eligible replacement. Under the program, the commissioner must require that:

(1) rebate applications include specifications about the equipment being replaced, the equipment being installed, the programming of the equipment being installed, and an estimate of the annual salt use of the newly installed equipment;

(2) contractors certify that the equipment will be installed and programmed in a manner that complies with this section;

(3) both the owner or lessee of the property and the contractor sign a rebate application;

(4) rebates will be sent to the owner or lessee of the property; and

(5) a contractor may sign no more than 30 rebate applications for the life of the program.

Sec. 2. APPROPRIATION; TIME-BASED WATER SOFTENER REPLACEMENT PROGRAM REBATES.

$....... in fiscal year 2026 is appropriated from the general fund to the commissioner of the Pollution Control Agency to issue rebates under the time-based water softener replacement program established under section 1. This is a onetime appropriation and is available until June 30, 2028.
